items.en: English adopts hydraulic and later builds water words on the same root.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 hydraulic，此后又用同一词根构造新的水相关词汇。

items.en: Words on -onic, from electronic, give a technical model for new system names.
items.cn: 以 electronic 为代表的 -onic 词尾，为新系统命名提供了技术化的构词模板。

items.en: Hydronic is coined in North American heating literature for water-based comfort systems.
items.cn: 现代英语中，北美供暖技术文献造出 hydronic 一词，指以水为介质的环境控制系统。

note.en: Hydronic looks like hydraulic and hydronics and belongs to the same water-root family, while standing close to words for systems that heat or cool a building.
note.cn: hydronic 与 hydraulic、hydronics 外形相近、同属「水」词根家族，同时与「建筑供暖制冷系统」一类词义场相邻。

entries.definition: the science of liquids in motion
entries.definitionCN: 水力学；研究运动液体的学科

entries.definition: the technology of water-based heating and cooling
entries.definitionCN: 水暖技术；液体循环供暖与制冷技术

entries.definition: to take in water
working by controlling small electric currents
entries.definitionCN: 电子的；靠控制微小电流工作的，是 -onic 词尾的构词样板

entries.definition: a system that heats a whole building from one source
a metal panel that gives out heat to a room
the pipes and systems that carry water in a building

normalIntro.en: Hydronic is the water root in a technical coat: whenever a building uses moving water to control temperature, the word applies.
normalIntro.cn: hydronic 是披上技术外衣的「水」词根：只要建筑靠流动的水控温，就可以用这个词。

normal.en: The root hydr- means water, as in hydrate and hydrogen.
normal.cn: 词根 hydr- 意为水，hydrate 与 hydrogen 中都有它。

normal.en: The ending -ic turns a root into an adjective describing a system.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ic 把词根变成描述系统的形容词。

normal.en: Hydraulic moves water to do work, while hydronic uses water to control temperature.
normal.cn: hydraulic 让水做功，hydronic 则用水控温。

normal.en: Hydronics is the trade name, so a hydronics engineer designs hydronic heating.
normal.cn: hydronics 是行业名称，因此水暖工程师设计的是 hydronic 供暖系统。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with electronic: the first two letters show water, not electricity.
normal.cn: 不要与 electronic 混淆：开头几个字母提示的是水，而不是电。

abstract.en: See faint red lines glowing under wooden floorboards as warm water runs through them.
abstract.cn: 想象木地板下方泛起淡淡的红光，热水正在细管里流动。

abstract.en: Imagine chilled water flowing through ceiling panels while the room slowly turns cool.
abstract.cn: 想象冷冻水流过吊顶板，房间慢慢转凉。

abstract.en: Picture a technician tracing a loop of pipe and writing down the water pressure.
abstract.cn: 想象一名技师沿着循环管路查看，并记下水压读数。

examples.en: Hydronic heating is quieter and more even than blowing warm air.
examples.cn: 水暖比吹热风更安静、更均匀。

examples.en: The old school replaced its steam pipes with a hydronic system.
examples.cn: 这所老学校把蒸汽管道换成了水暖系统。

examples.en: Many hydronic installations now use a small heat pump.
examples.cn: 如今许多水暖装置使用小型热泵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨，做梦」——冬天靠热水循环，屋里暖得像做梦；这只是谐音联想，与希腊语词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hydor（水）→ 构词成分 hydr-（水）+ 技术性形容词词尾 -ic → 英语 hydronic（用水循环供暖或制冷的）。

sensesIntro.en: Hydronic first describes water-based heating, then the same water loop used for cooling, and finally the whole trade of designing such systems.
sensesIntro.cn: hydronic 先指以水供暖，再指同一套水路用于制冷，最后扩展到设计这类系统的整个行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: warm water running in loops beneath a floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：热水在地板下的管路中循环。

branches.en: Water carrying heat into a building is the main sense.
branches.cn: 把热量送进建筑是主要义项。

branches.en: Water carrying heat away gives the cooling sense.
branches.cn: 让水带走热量就形成制冷义项。

branches.en: The noun field name covers the whole trade.
branches.cn: 名词化的行业名称覆盖整个手艺领域。

branches.en: Heating and cooling share the same closed water loop.
branches.cn: 供暖与制冷共用同一个封闭水路。

branches.en: Cooling jobs are part of the hydronics trade.
branches.cn: 制冷工程也属于水暖行业的工作范围。

intro.en: Hydronic is made of the water root hydr-, a linking -on, and the adjective ending -ic, the same pattern that builds hydraulics and electronics.
intro.cn: hydronic 由「水」词根 hydr-、连接成分 -on 与形容词词尾 -ic 组成，hydraulics 与 electronics 也采用类似的构词方式。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek: hydor means water, though Latin borrowed the same stem in hydraulicus before English took it over.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自希腊语：hydor 意为水；拉丁语在 hydraulicus 中借用了同一词干，英语再由其传入。

items.example: The root hydr- begins the word hydronic.
items.exampleCN: 词根 hydr- 是 hydronic 的开头。

items.example: The linking -on appears in hydronics.
items.exampleCN: 连接成分 -on 出现在 hydronics 中。

items.meaning: relating to, of the nature of
items.meaningCN: 表示有关的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ic forms hydronic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 hydronic。

items.meaning: the science of liquids in motion
items.example: Hydraulics shares the water root.
items.exampleCN: hydraulics 共享「水」词根。

items.example: Hydronics names the trade itself.
items.exampleCN: hydronics 指这一行业本身。

items.example: Hydrate also carries the water root.
items.exampleCN: hydrate 同样带着「水」词根。

items.meaning: the study of water on earth
items.example: Hydrology studies rivers and rain.
items.exampleCN: 水文学研究河流与降水。

items.example: The suffix -ics forms hydronics.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ics 构成 hydronics。

items.meaning: a device that holds a set temperature
items.example: A thermostat controls the hydronic loop.
items.exampleCN: 温控器控制着水暖回路。

definition_zh: 水听器；水下听音器
definition_en: a device that picks up sound under water and turns it into an electric signal
core_image: 一只沉进水里的耳朵，把水下的声响收进来
scene: 科考船放下探听装置，海豚在船边发出一串咔嗒声。水听器把这些声音录了下来。The hydrophone stayed in the water all night and recorded every dolphin call.
sceneCN: 这里 hydrophone 是「水听器」（第 1 个义项：把水下声音变成电信号的仪器）；句意：水听器把海豚发出的那串声音录了下来。

pos.zh: 水听器；水下听音器

collocations.zh: 给水听器加挡板隔离干扰

derivatives.zh: 与水听器有关的；由 -ic 加在名词后构成形容词
装了水听器的；动词化后加 -ed 构成
水下声响探测；以 -y 结尾的抽象名词

senses.title: A listening device for under water
senses.definition: an instrument that catches sound waves under water and converts them into electrical signals
senses.definitionCN: 捕捉水下声波并把它转换成电信号的仪器
senses.example: The research team lowered a hydrophone beside the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 研究团队在礁石旁放下了一只水听器。
senses.why: Greek hudor means water and phone means sound, so the word names a sound catcher that works where human ears barely manage.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 hudor 意为「水」，phone 意为「声音」，所以这个词说的是一种在人类耳朵几乎无能为力的地方捕捉声音的装置。

senses.title: The recorded sounds themselves
senses.definition: the audio track or data file gathered with such a device, especially by marine biologists
senses.definitionCN: 用这类装置采集到的音频或数据文件，尤指海洋生物学者取得的声音
senses.example: Her hydrophone of the night chorus lasted four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她那晚录到的夜唱水听录音长达四个小时。
senses.why: Once the device becomes an everyday tool, people start naming the material it collects with the same word, much as a film can mean the object or the footage.
senses.whyCN: 当装置成为日常工具后，人们会用同一个词来称呼它收集到的内容，就像 film 既可指胶片也可指胶片上的影片。

senses.title: A sensor in seismic surveys
senses.definition: a pressure sensor towed in oil and gas surveys that hears echoes bouncing back from rock layers below the seabed
senses.definitionCN: 油气勘探中拖在船后的压力传感器，收听从海床下方岩层反射回来的回声
senses.example: The survey ship streams a hydrophone behind it all day.
senses.exampleCN: 勘探船整天在船后拖着一只水听器。
senses.why: Seafloor geology is explored with the same trick as whale watching: make a bang, then listen for the echo, so marine and industrial service share the device.
senses.whyCN: 探索海底地质和观察鲸类用的是同一招：先制造一声巨响，再听回声，因此海洋研究与工业勘探共用这件设备。

intro.en: Hydrophone combines Greek hudor, water, with phone, sound or voice.
intro.cn: hydrophone 由希腊语 hudor（水）与 phone（声音、嗓音）组合而成。

items.en: Hudor means water, and phone means a sound or a voice.
items.cn: hudor 意为水，phone 意为声音或嗓音。

items.en: A device for hearing under water is first described in the middle of the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪中叶，英国文献首次描述用于水下听音的装置。

items.en: Military listening gear puts the combining form hydro- next to phone.
items.cn: 军事听音设备把构词成分 hydro- 与 phone 拼在一起。

items.en: Submarine warfare gives the instrument a fixed, technical sense.
items.cn: 潜艇战让这件仪器获得固定的技术含义。

items.en: Marine biology, seismology, and wildlife law now use it for microphones that work in water.
items.cn: 如今海洋生物学、地震学与野生动物保护法令都用它指能在水中工作的麦克风。

note.en: Hydrophone sits in the tribe of -phone instruments, beside microphones, geophones, and the Greek word for water.
note.cn: hydrophone 属于以 -phone 结尾的器材一族，与 microphone、geophone 以及希腊语中表示「水」的词相邻。

entries.definition: a device that picks up sound in air
a sensor that hears vibrations in rock or soil
entries.definitionCN: 监听岩土振动的检波仪

entries.definition: a shortened English form referring to water power
entries.definitionCN: 英语缩略形式，指水力发电

entries.definition: equipment that sends pulses under water and reads the echoes
entries.definitionCN: 在水中发出声脉冲并读取回声的设备

entries.definition: the science of sound travelling through water
any equipment used to hear sounds nearby
entries.definitionCN: 任何用来听取附近声音的设备

normalIntro.en: Hydrophone is built like microphone: hydro is water, phone is sound, so it is a microphone that dives.
normalIntro.cn: hydrophone 像 microphone 那样构词：hydro 是水，phone 是声音，所以它就是会潜水的麦克风。

normal.en: Swap micro for hydro and the microphone goes under water.
normal.cn: 把 micro 换成 hydro，这只麦克风就下水了。

normal.en: A hydrophone array is a row of them, so a wide stretch of sea is heard at once.
normal.cn: 「」串成一排，就能同时听取一大片海域的声音。

normal.en: The word behaves like microphone and geophone, so the plural simply adds s.
normal.cn: 这个词的用法与 microphone、geophone 一致，所以复数直接在词尾加 s。

normal.en: Marine biologists lower one to hear whales; survey ships tow one to hear the seabed.
normal.cn: 海洋生物学者放下去听鲸叫；勘探船拖着它听海床的回声。

normal.en: Remember that phone here is sound, not telephone, so the word never needs a second n.
normal.cn: 要记住这里的 phone 是「声音」而不是「电话」，所以拼写里不需要再多个 n。

abstract.en: Picture a glass bell dropped into dark water, a small light blinking as sound arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃钟沉入黑暗的水里，有声音传来时里面亮起一点闪光。

abstract.en: Imagine a whale song saved as a wavy line on a screen and filed away like a voice message.
abstract.cn: 想象一段鲸歌变成屏幕上的波浪线，像语音留言一样被存档。

abstract.en: Think of a ship dragging a chain of ears behind it over the seabed.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船在身后拖着一串耳朵，缓缓掠过海床。

examples.en: Whale songs were captured on a hydrophone anchored to the sea floor.
examples.cn: 鲸歌被一只固定在海底的水听器录了下来。

examples.en: The noise of the passing ferry drowned out the hydrophones for ten minutes.
examples.cn: 路过的渡轮噪声让水听器失灵了十分钟。

examples.en: Before the survey began, the crew checked that every hydrophone was working.
examples.cn: 勘测开始前，船员检查了每个水听器是否工作正常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海卓风」——海上的微风钻进耳朵，就是听水声的装置；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hudor（水）→ hydro-（水；液）+ 希腊语 phone（声音）→ hydrophone（水听器），核心义「在水里接收声音」。

sensesIntro.en: Hydrophone names the instrument first, then the recording it makes, and finally its specialist role in oil and gas surveys.
sensesIntro.cn: hydrophone 先指仪器本身，再指它录下的声音，最后指它在油气勘探中担起的专门角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ear sunk below the surface, turning the sounds of water into a signal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只沉在水下的耳朵，把水的声响变成信号。

branches.en: The instrument sense is the everyday scientific meaning.
branches.cn: 仪器义项是日常科研中的主要含义。

branches.en: The recording sense names what the instrument captures.
branches.cn: 录音义项指仪器所采集的内容。

branches.en: The survey sense narrows the instrument to industrial use.
branches.cn: 勘探义项把仪器限定在工业用途上。

branches.en: Both meanings listen for echoes, one from whales and one from rock.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在听回声，一个来自鲸，一个来自岩石。

branches.en: A hydrophone array and its recording feed the same wildlife studies.
branches.cn: 水听器阵列与其录音共同服务于同样的野生动物研究。

intro.en: Hydrophone is a modern compound of hydro-, water, and -phone, sound, so its pieces are easy to name.
intro.cn: hydrophone 是 hydro-（水）与 -phone（声音）组成的现代复合词，两部分的含义都很清楚。

latinIntro.en: Both elements come from Greek, so the Latin relatives are listed only as notes on the Greek origin.
latinIntro.cn: 两个构词成分都源自希腊语，所以这里只说明其希腊文来源。

items.example: Hydro- links the device to water.
items.exampleCN: hydro- 把装置与水联系起来。

items.example: The suffix -phone tells you what is captured.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -phone 说明它捕捉的是什么。

items.meaning: a device for hearing under water
items.example: A hydrophone receives sound already in water.
items.exampleCN: hydrophone 接收本就存在于水中的声音。

items.example: The suffix -s makes hydrophones.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 hydrophones。

items.meaning: a device for hearing in air
items.example: Microphone shares the suffix and the shape.
items.exampleCN: microphone 同用这个词尾，形状相同。

items.meaning: a device for hearing in ground
items.example: Geophone swaps water for earth.
items.exampleCN: geophone 把「水」换成了「土」。

items.meaning: a device for hearing a voice from far away
items.example: Telephone uses rame sound across a distance.
items.exampleCN: telephone 把声音送往远方。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms hydrophonic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 hydrophonic。

items.meaning: a device that puts out sound
items.example: Loudspeaker plays the opposite role of a hydrophone.
items.exampleCN: loudspeaker 所扮的角色正好相反。

definition_zh: 双曲线；双曲线轨迹
definition_en: a curve of two open branches, each bending away from the centre forever
core_image: 两片向外张开的弧线，越伸越远，永不闭合
scene: 把冷却塔放到侧光里，只见两道曲线对称上扬，越往上越向外张开。塔身侧影就是一道张开的曲线。The side of a cooling tower follows the same hyperbola from top to bottom.
sceneCN: 这里 hyperbola 是「双曲线」（第 1 个义项：平面上两支对称张开的曲线）；句意：冷却塔之所以呈这种弧度，是因为每道混凝土线都沿着同一条双曲线。

pos.zh: 双曲线；双曲线轨迹

derivatives.zh: 双曲线的；以 -ic 加在名词后构成形容词
双曲面；加 -oid（像……的东西）构成
沿双曲线地；如双曲线地；由形容词加 -ly 构成

senses.title: The two branched curve
senses.definition: a plane curve made of two open branches whose points are all at a fixed distance difference from two fixed points
senses.definitionCN: 平面上由两支张开曲线组成的图形，其上每一点到两个定点的距离之差都相等
senses.example: A circle closes, but a hyperbola never meets itself again.
senses.exampleCN: 圆会闭合，而双曲线永不与自己重逢。
senses.why: Greek hyperballein means to throw beyond or overshoot, and the curve keeps overshooting its centre, so the name pictures a throw that goes past the mark.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 hyperballein 意为「扔过头、越过」，而这条曲线恰恰一直越过中心，所以名字里的画面就是一次投掷扔过了目标。

senses.title: The orbit of a passing comet
senses.definition: the path traced by a body moving fast enough to swing past a star once and leave, never returning
senses.definitionCN: 运动速度足够快的天体绕过恒星一次便离去、永不复返的轨迹
senses.example: The comet follows a hyperbola and will not come back.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗彗星沿双曲线运行，不会再回来。
senses.why: When speed exceeds the escape speed, an ellipse stretches until it breaks open into two branches, so the curve becomes the shape of a one time visit.
senses.whyCN: 当速度超过逃逸速度，椭圆就被拉断成两支张开的曲线，于是这条曲线成了「只来一次」的形状。

senses.title: Echoes that miss the focus
senses.definition: the curved echo trail produced on a ground radar or seismic record when a buried object is not exactly under the sensor
senses.definitionCN: 地面雷达或地震记录中，埋藏物不在传感器正下方时出现的那道弯曲回声
senses.example: Each buried pipe showed up as a small hyperbola on the record.
senses.exampleCN: 每根埋管在记录上都显示成一道小双曲线。
senses.why: The distance to the target changes with every step of the sensor, and the graph of that distance against time is literally the curve, so survey picking became a name.
senses.whyCN: 传感器每移动一步，到目标的距离都会改变，把距离对时间作图得到的正是这条曲线，于是「拾取双曲线」成了行业里的说法。

intro.en: Hyperbola is Greek in origin: hyper, beyond, plus ballein, to throw, because the curve is thrown beyond the cone and closes nothing.
intro.cn: hyperbola 源自希腊语：hyper 表示「越过」，ballein 意为「投掷」，因为这条曲线投过了圆锥，什么也闭合不了。

items.en: Ballein means to throw, and hyper means beyond.
items.cn: ballein 意为投掷，hyper 意为越过。

items.en: Apollonius of Perga cuts a cone at different angles and calls the widest section a hyperbola.
items.cn: 公元前三世纪，佩尔加的阿波罗尼奥斯用不同角度切圆锥，把最外的一种截面称作 hyperbola。

items.en: Renaissance scholars take the Greek name into Latin as hyperbola.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的学者把这个希腊词名以 hyperbola 的形式带入拉丁语。

items.en: The conic name enters English while the older rhetoric word hyperbole keeps a different spelling.
items.cn: 这个圆锥曲线的名称进入英语，与更早的修辞词 hyperbole 保持不同拼写。

items.en: Analytic geometry and survey geophysics add equations, asymptotes, and radar hyperbolas.
items.cn: 解析几何与勘探地球物理为它增添了方程、渐近线和雷达双曲线。

note.en: Hyperbola looks like hyperbole, though the maths curve and the figure of speech parted ways in spelling centuries ago.
note.cn: hyperbola 与 hyperbole 形近，但这条数学曲线与那种修辞格在拼写上早已分道扬镳。

entries.definition: deliberate exaggeration, such as a flood of tears
entries.definitionCN: 夸张修辞；只是拼写相近，词源虽同却已分化为不同词

entries.definition: relating to a hyperbola, or wildly exaggerated
entries.definitionCN: 双曲线的；也常指夸张的

entries.definition: a three dimensional surface swept by rotating a hyperbola
entries.definitionCN: 双曲线绕轴旋转形成的双曲面

entries.definition: a closed oval curve, the shape of a planet orbit
entries.definitionCN: 闭合的椭圆曲线，即行星轨道形状

entries.definition: an open curve with one branch, the path of a thrown ball
entries.definitionCN: 只有一支的开放曲线，即抛球的轨迹

entries.definition: a straight line that a curve approaches but never touches
entries.definitionCN: 曲线不断接近却永不触及的直线

normalIntro.en: Hyperbola and hyperbole share Greek hyper, beyond, so both words carry too far; the maths one is the curve thrown past the cone.
normalIntro.cn: hyperbola 与 hyperbole 都有希腊语 hyper（越过），两者都「过了头」；其中数学的那一个是投过圆锥的曲线。

normal.en: The ending is -bola, not -bole, so the curve and the figure of speech stay apart.
normal.cn: 词尾是 -bola 而不是 -bole，曲线与夸张修辞由此分开。

normal.en: A hyperbola has two branches and two asymptotes, and the branches hug the asymptotes as they leave.
normal.cn: 双曲线有两支和两条渐近线，两支在远去时不断贴近渐近线。

normal.en: The rectangular kind has perpendicular asymptotes and is the graph of a simple inverse relation.
normal.cn: 等轴双曲线的两条渐近线互相垂直，是简单反比例关系的图像。

normal.en: Compare parabola, which keeps one branch; hyperbola splits into two.
normal.cn: 对比 parabola：抛物线只有一支，双曲线分成两支。

normal.en: Hyperbolic is both the adjective of the curve and the adjective of exaggeration, so context decides.
normal.cn: hyperbolic 既是「双曲线的」，也是「夸张的」，要看上下文分辨。

abstract.en: Picture two thin ribbons flung from one point and flying off in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象两条细丝带从一点甩出，朝相反方向飞走。

abstract.en: Imagine a comet whipping round the sun once and streaking away for good.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗彗星绕太阳掠过一次，然后一去不返。

abstract.en: See a radar screen where a buried pipe leaves a shallow arch that never closes.
abstract.cn: 想象雷达屏幕上，一根埋管留下一道浅浅的拱弧，始终没有闭合。

examples.en: The cooling tower has the shape of a hyperbola from the side.
examples.cn: 冷却塔从侧面看是双曲线的形状。

examples.en: Students drew the hyperbola and then marked both asymptotes.
examples.cn: 学生们画出了双曲线，然后标出两条渐近线。

examples.en: A body flying faster than escape speed follows an open path, not a closed loop.
examples.cn: 速度超过逃逸速度的天体走的是开放路径，而不是闭合轨道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「还怕勒」——两根曲线越拉越远，像绳子被勒到极限也不肯合拢；这纯属谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hyper-（越过；超出）+ ballein（投掷）→ 希腊语 hyperbole（投过头）→ 拉丁语·新拉丁语 hyperbola → 英语 hyperbola，核心义「投过圆锥、永不合拢的曲线」。

sensesIntro.en: Hyperbola starts as a pure geometric curve, then lends its shape to comet orbits and finally to curved echo trails on survey records.
sensesIntro.cn: hyperbola 起初是一条纯几何曲线，随后把形状借给彗星轨道，最后又用来形容勘探记录上弯曲的回声轨迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arcs thrown outward from the centre, spreading wider and wider without ever closing.
core.cn: 核心意象：两段从中心往外甩出的弧线，越张越开，始终不合拢。

branches.en: The geometric curve is the original and most familiar sense.
branches.cn: 几何曲线是最原始也最熟悉的义项。

branches.en: Comet paths apply the curve to the sky.
branches.cn: 彗星轨道把这条曲线用到了天上。

branches.en: Survey echoes use the curve as a reading pattern.
branches.cn: 勘探回声把这条曲线用作读数图样。

branches.en: An orbit and a drawn curve are one shape in two places.
branches.cn: 一条轨道与一条画出的曲线是同一形状出现在两处。

branches.en: Radar picks the arch because it resembles the drawn curve.
branches.cn: 雷达之所以能找出那道弧，是因为它形似画出的曲线。

intro.en: Hyperbola is built from the Greek prefix hyper-, beyond, and the Greek verb ballein, to throw.
intro.cn: hyperbola 由希腊语前缀 hyper-（越过）与希腊语动词 ballein（投掷）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form hyperbola was taken from Greek during the Renaissance, so the Latin relatives are listed as a short note.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 hyperbola 是文艺复兴时期从希腊语引入的，这里只作简短说明。

items.example: Hyper- marks a curve thrown beyond the cone.
items.exampleCN: hyper- 表明这条曲线投过了圆锥。

items.example: The element -bola comes from the verb meaning to throw.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -bola 来自表示投掷的动词。

items.example: A hyperbola has asymptotes that it never meets.
items.exampleCN: 双曲线有永不触及的渐近线。

items.example: The suffix -s makes hyperbolas.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 hyperbolas。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms hyperbolic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 hyperbolic。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms hyperboloid.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oid 构成 hyperboloid。

items.example: Parabola uses the same Greek ending.
items.exampleCN: parabola 使用相同的希腊语词尾。

items.example: Ellipse is the closed member of the same family.
items.exampleCN: ellipse 是同一家族中闭合的那种。

items.example: Asymptote always travels with a hyperbola.
items.exampleCN: asymptote 总与双曲线同行。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 开放的圆锥截面；双曲线

definition_zh: 恶性通货膨胀；极度通货膨胀
definition_en: very fast and out of control inflation, in which prices rise month after month
core_image: 钞票上的数字一路加零，车轮越转越快
scene: 面包店一天改好几次价签，人们推着车子去买米。物价与钞票一同失控。That hyperinflation left the city with savings worth less than the paper they were printed on.
sceneCN: 这里 hyperinflation 是「恶性通货膨胀」（第 1 个义项：物价失控暴涨、货币迅速贬值的现象）；句意：那场恶性通货膨胀让整座城市的积蓄变得比印钞的纸还不值钱。

pos.zh: 恶性通货膨胀；极度通货膨胀

collocations.zh: 恶性通货膨胀不断失控
恶性通货膨胀开始蔓延
一段恶性通货膨胀的时期

derivatives.zh: 恶性通货膨胀的；加 -ary 构成形容词
使急剧膨胀；由 -in- 加 -flate（吹起）构成
恶性膨胀的；加 -ed 构成形容词

senses.title: Prices rising out of control
senses.definition: a very high and self feeding rise in prices that money can no longer keep up with
senses.definitionCN: 物价极高且不断自我强化的上涨，货币已完全追不上
senses.example: Wages were paid twice a day during the hyperinflation.
senses.exampleCN: 恶性通货膨胀期间，工资一天发两次。
senses.why: The Greek prefix hyper- means beyond, so the word puts ordinary inflation past breaking point, where rising prices feed on themselves.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语前缀 hyper- 表示「越过」，因此这个词把普通的通货膨胀推过了崩坏的临界点，物价越涨越是互相催动。

senses.title: Money that people no longer trust
senses.definition: the collapse of confidence in a currency, so people spend or trade it as fast as they can
senses.definitionCN: 人们对货币信心崩溃，争相花掉或换成其他东西的状态
senses.example: Hyperinflation turned banknotes into fuel for the stove.
senses.exampleCN: 恶性通货膨胀让钞票沦为了炉膛里的燃料。
senses.why: When the same sum buys less by the hour, holding money becomes a loss, so the social side of the term is a rush to get rid of cash.
senses.whyCN: 当同样的钱每小时都买到更少的东西，持有货币就变成了亏损，于是这个词的社会一面就是人们急着把现金甩出去。

senses.title: A metaphor for runaway growth
senses.definition: a joking or critical way to describe anything multiplying far too fast, such as clickbait headlines or jargon
senses.definitionCN: 调侃或批评某事物过快增多，如标题党文章或术语的泛滥
senses.example: The hyperinflation of buzzwords makes reports unreadable.
senses.exampleCN: 术语的恶性膨胀让报告变得难以卒读。
senses.why: Because the word pictures numbers climbing without limit, it borrows easily to name any quantity that grows faster than the thing it measures.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词画出的画面是数字无限攀升，所以它很容易被借去指任何涨得比被计量的东西还快的数量。

intro.en: Hyperinflation is a twentieth century compound of the Latin prefix meaning beyond and the Latin verb meaning to blow into.
intro.cn: hyperinflation 是二十世纪形成的复合词，由表示「越过」的拉丁语前缀与表示「吹进」的拉丁语动词拼成。

items.en: Inflare means to blow into or puff up, and flare means to blow.
items.cn: inflare 意为吹入、吹胀，flare 意为吹。

items.en: The prefix hyper- comes from Greek, meaning over or beyond.
items.cn: 前缀 hyper- 来自希腊语，意为越过、超出。

items.en: Inflation begins to mean a general rise in prices.
items.cn: 十九世纪，inflation 开始表示物价普遍上涨。

items.en: Economists describing Germany and Hungary add hyper- to make the severity explicit.
items.cn: 二十世纪，形容德国与匈牙利局势的经济学家加上 hyper-，以彰显其严重程度。

items.en: The term spreads to Latin America and beyond, and to loose figurative uses.
items.cn: 此后该词流传到拉丁美洲等地，也出现了宽泛的比喻用法。

note.en: Hyperinflation shares a family with inflation, deflation, and stagflation, and is widely mistaken for the maths word hyperbola.
note.cn: hyperinflation 与 inflation、deflation、stagflation 同属一族，也常被人们误当成数学词 hyperbola。

entries.definition: a general rise in prices
relating to a maths curve, or wildly exaggerated
entries.definitionCN: 与 hyperinflation 只是前缀抬头相似，词源不同：它指双曲线的或夸张的

entries.definition: unusually restless and busy
a general fall in prices
rising prices together with slow growth
entries.definitionCN: 物价上涨而经济增长停滞

entries.definition: the moment a money stops working

normalIntro.en: Hyperinflation is just inflation with the Greek prefix that means beyond, so it names prices that have blown past every limit.
normalIntro.cn: hyperinflation 就是在 inflation 前面加上意为「越过」的希腊语前缀，所以它指的是涨过了一切界限的物价。

normal.en: Inflation puffs prices up, and hyperinflation puffs them past the point of control.
normal.cn: inflation 把物价吹起来，hyperinflation 则把它吹到失去控制。

normal.en: The base verb inflate comes from Latin flare, to blow, so the whole family breathes air.
normal.cn: 基础动词 inflate 源自拉丁语 flare（吹），所以这一词族都与「吹气」有关。

normal.en: De-, in-, and hyper- mark the direction: down, in, and far beyond.
normal.cn: 前缀 de-、in-、hyper- 表明方向：往下、往内、远远超出。

normal.en: The word is uncountable, so it appears without an article in most sentences.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数，多数情况下句中不带冠词。

normal.en: The adjective hyperinflationary keeps the whole stem and adds -ary.
normal.cn: 形容词 hyperinflationary 保留整个词干，再加 -ary。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag with a new zero glued on every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签，每天早晨都被加上一个新的零。

abstract.en: Imagine paper money stuffed into a stove because it burns cheaper than coal.
abstract.cn: 想象钞票被塞进炉子，因为烧它比烧煤还便宜。

abstract.en: See a balloon blown so large that every word it carries is now overpriced.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被吹得过大的气球，上面写着的每个词都开始漫天要价。

examples.en: Hyperinflation wiped out the savings of an entire generation.
examples.cn: 恶性通货膨胀抹去了整整一代人的积蓄。

examples.en: The central bank was still fighting hyperinflation a decade later.
examples.cn: 十年之后，中央银行仍在与恶性通货膨胀作斗争。

examples.en: Historians study old banknotes to measure how long each burst of price rises lasted.
examples.cn: 历史学家研究旧钞，以衡量每一轮物价上涨持续了多久。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「还怕」再「放大」——物价还怕不够高，一再放大，就是恶性膨胀；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hyper-（越过）＋ 拉丁语 in-（向内）+ flare（吹）→ 英语 inflate（充气；膨胀）→ inflation（通货膨胀）→ 再加 hyper- 构成 hyperinflation，核心义「涨过一切界限」。

sensesIntro.en: Hyperinflation first names the price spiral itself, then the collapse of trust in money, and finally any runaway growth used loosely.
sensesIntro.cn: hyperinflation 先指物价螺旋本身，再指货币信任的崩塌，最后泛指任何失控的膨胀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: digits on a banknote growing a new zero while the wheel of prices spins faster and faster.
core.cn: 核心意象：钞票上的数字不断加零，物价的车轮越转越快。

branches.en: The economic spiral is the defining sense.
branches.cn: 经济螺旋是这个词的定义性义项。

branches.en: Lost trust in money is the social consequence.
branches.cn: 货币信任的丧失是社会层面的后果。

branches.en: Loose growth is the figurative extension.
branches.cn: 宽泛的膨胀是比喻性延伸。

branches.en: Rising prices and lost trust keep each other going.
branches.cn: 物价上涨与信任丧失互为因果、彼此推动。

branches.en: Both senses describe a quantity growing beyond its measure.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述某数量涨得超过了它的尺度。

intro.en: Hyperinflation stacks three pieces: hyper-, in-, and -flation, all built on the Latin verb for blowing.
intro.cn: hyperinflation 叠了三个成分：hyper-、in- 与 -flation，它们都建在表示「吹」的拉丁语动词之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare means to blow, inflare means to blow into, and the prefix hyper- was borrowed from Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flare 意为吹，inflare 意为吹入，而前缀 hyper- 是从希腊语借来的。

items.example: Hyper- pushes the word past normal limits.
items.exampleCN: hyper- 把这个词推过了正常界限。

items.example: In- says the air is blown inward.
items.exampleCN: in- 表示气被吹了进去。

items.example: Flare is the breath behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: flare 是整个词族的「一口气」。

items.meaning: to fill with air or expand
items.example: Inflate means to blow something up.
items.exampleCN: inflate 意为把某物吹起来。

items.example: Inflation adds -ion to the verb.
items.exampleCN: inflation 在动词后加 -ion。

items.example: The suffix -ion makes the verb a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 把动词变成名词。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms hyperinflationary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成 hyperinflationary。

items.example: Deflation turns the prefix the other way.
items.exampleCN: deflation 把前缀的方向反了过来。

items.meaning: a policy of pushing prices back up
items.example: Reflation swaps in a different prefix only.
items.exampleCN: reflation 只不过换了另一个前缀。

definition_zh: 催眠的；令人昏昏欲睡的；引人入胜的；催眠药
definition_en: relating to hypnosis, or able to hold attention so strongly that it seems like a trance
core_image: 钟摆在眼前来回摇，眼皮越来越沉
scene: 剧场灯光渐暗，鼓点一下一下敲着。The steady drumbeat in the dark hall was so hypnotic that the audience forgot to breathe.
sceneCN: 这里 hypnotic 是「令人着迷的、引人入胜的」（第 3 个义项：牢牢吸住注意力）；句意：昏暗大厅里单调的鼓点如此引人入胜，观众连呼吸都忘了。

pos.zh: 催眠的；令人昏昏欲睡的；引人入胜的
催眠药；安眠药（多用于复数）

derivatives.zh: 由希腊词根 hypnos（睡眠）加 -osis（状态）构成，义为「催眠状态」
由 hypnotic 换 -ize（使……化）构成，义为「对……施行催眠术」
形容词加 -ally 构成的副词，义为「以催眠的方式」
加 -ism（做法、体系）构成，义为「催眠术」
加 -ist（从事者）构成，义为「催眠师」

senses.title: Relating to hypnosis
senses.definition: connected with the practice of putting a person into a sleep-like state under control
senses.definitionCN: 与把人带入受控的半睡眠状态的催眠术有关的
senses.example: The doctor used hypnotic suggestion to ease her fear.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用催眠暗示来缓解她的恐惧。
senses.why: Hypnos, the Greek god of sleep, sleeps inside the word; anything of hypnosis keeps that sleep image.
senses.whyCN: 希腊睡神许普诺斯的名字就睡在词里，凡属催眠的事物都保留着「入睡」的画面。

senses.title: Making people sleepy
senses.definition: causing a person to feel drowsy and relax out of ordinary awareness
senses.definitionCN: 使人昏昏欲睡、放松到失去平常的警觉
senses.example: The warm room and soft music were hypnotic after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭后温暖的房间和轻柔的音乐让人昏昏欲睡。
senses.why: The same trance state becomes an everyday effect when a soft rhythm or stuffy room slowly shuts the mind down.
senses.whyCN: 同样一种恍惚状态，一旦遇上柔和节拍或沉闷房间，就变成了让脑子慢慢关机的日常效果。

senses.title: Holding attention like a spell
senses.titleCN: 引人入胜的；令人着迷的
senses.definition: so fascinating that attention is fixed and ordinary thinking fades
senses.definitionCN: 迷人到注意力被牢牢固定、寻常思绪退去的
senses.example: Her hypnotic gaze held the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种令人着迷的目光吸引了全场。
senses.why: A hypnotized person cannot look away from the swing of the object, and this image easily widens to any art that fixes the eye.
senses.whyCN: 被催眠的人无法从摇动物体上移开视线，这一画面很容易扩展为任何牢牢抓住视线的艺术。

senses.title: A sleep-inducing drug
senses.definition: a medicine that brings on sleep, usually used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 能催人入睡的药物，通常用复数
senses.example: The nurse gave the patient a mild hypnotic.
senses.exampleCN: 护士给病人服用了一种温和的催眠药。
senses.why: Once the adjective names whatever brings sleep, it also names the drug itself as a stand-alone noun.
senses.whyCN: 形容词既能指带来睡眠的东西，也就顺理成章地独立成名词，指药物本身。

intro.en: Hypnotic goes back to Greek hypnos, sleep, the name of the god Hypnos, and to hypnos, a sleep-inducing plant, used by doctors in the eighteen hundreds.
intro.cn: hypnotic 上溯至希腊语 hypnos（睡眠，也是睡神的名字），以及十九世纪医生所用以催眠的植物。

items.en: Hypnos names the god of sleep and also means sleep itself.
items.cn: hypnos 既是睡神之名，也直接表示睡眠。

items.en: Doctors adopt hypnotism as a term for the sleep-like trance they produce.
items.cn: 十九世纪四十年代，医生用 hypnotism 指他们制造出的似睡恍惚状态。

items.en: The adjective hypnotic is formed on the model of hypnotism.
items.cn: 英语仿 hypnotism 造出形容词 hypnotic。

items.en: The new doctors of the mind give the word its medical sense.
items.cn: 新兴的精神医生赋予这个词医学含义。

items.en: The word widens to any rhythm or spell that holds attention.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到一切抓住注意力的节奏或魔力。

note.en: Hypnotic shares the sleep root with hypnosis and hypnotize, and sits near words for sleepy effects and for fascination.
note.cn: hypnotic 与 hypnosis、hypnotize 共享「睡眠」词根，又与「令人困倦」和「令人着迷」两类词相邻。

entries.definition: a sleep-like state produced by suggestion
to put a person into a hypnotic state
a person who practises hypnosis
having lower osmotic pressure; only looks similar, different root
entries.definitionCN: 低渗的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: holding attention in a trance-like way
entries.definitionCN: 令人着迷的；令人恍惚的

entries.definition: making a person calm and sleepy
tending to cause sleep

normalIntro.en: Hypnotic looks back to Hypnos, the sleep god, and forward to the trance, the drowsiness, and the spell.
normalIntro.cn: hypnotic 向后望向睡神许普诺斯，向前伸向恍惚、困倦与魔力三层意思。

normal.en: Greek hypnos means sleep, and Hypnos is the name of the sleep god.
normal.cn: 希腊语 hypnos 意为睡眠，也是睡神的名字。

normal.en: Hypnosis, hypnotize, and hypnotist form one family around the same sleep root.
normal.cn: hypnosis、hypnotize、hypnotist 围绕同一个「睡眠」词根构成一个词族。

normal.en: The adjective ending -ic means having the nature of, as in hypnotic.
normal.cn: 形容词词尾 -ic 表示「具有……性质的」，hypnotic 就是最直接的例子。

normal.en: Hypnotic effect and hypnotic suggestion are fixed medical collocations.
normal.cn: hypnotic effect 与 hypnotic suggestion 是固定的医学术语搭配。

normal.en: Compare soporific, which also means sleep-inducing but sounds much more formal.
normal.cn: 对比 soporific：同样表示催眠，但语气正式得多。

abstract.en: Picture a watch swinging before your eyes in a dim room.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗房间里一块怀表在眼前来回摇摆。

abstract.en: Think of a voice that keeps repeating until the room grows heavy.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音反复念着，直到整间屋子变得沉甸甸。

abstract.en: Imagine not being able to look away from a bright spinning light.
abstract.cn: 想象眼前有团旋转的亮光，你怎么也移不开眼睛。

examples.en: The dancer moved with a hypnotic grace.
examples.cn: 那位舞者动作优雅，令人着迷。

examples.en: His hypnotic voice made the lecture feel like a dream.
examples.cn: 他那动人的嗓音让讲座像一场梦。

examples.en: The regular beat of the tide had a hypnotic effect on us.
examples.cn: 潮水规律的节拍对我们有一种催眠作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「希普诺提克」——希普诺斯是睡神，他提着油灯一晃，人就恍惚了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hypnos（睡眠，睡神许普诺斯）＋ 后缀 -ic（具有……性质的）→ hypnotic，核心义「使人进入睡眠般的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Hypnotic starts from the medical trance, turns into the drowsy feeling of ordinary life, and finally extends to any art that fixes attention.
sensesIntro.cn: hypnotic 从医学上的催眠术出发，转为日常生活中那种昏沉欲睡的感觉，最后扩展到牢牢抓住注意力的任何艺术。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pocket watch swinging before heavy eyelids.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只怀表在沉重的眼皮前摇动。

branches.en: The sense tied to hypnosis is the medical right edge of the chain.
branches.cn: 与催眠术相连的义项是语义链最右端的医学术语。

branches.en: Everyday drowsiness is the trance image softened.
branches.cn: 日常困倦是恍惚画面被柔化后的结果。

branches.en: Fascination is the trance image widened to art and atmosphere.
branches.cn: 引人入胜是把恍惚画面扩展到艺术与氛围。

branches.en: Both a spell and a practiced trance fix the mind on one point.
branches.cn: 魔法与熟练的催眠都把心神固定在一个点上。

branches.en: A sleep drug and a drowsy rhythm both pull the mind toward sleep.
branches.cn: 安眠药与催人欲睡的节奏都把心神拉向睡眠。

intro.en: Hypnotic joins the Greek root hyp- / hypn-, meaning sleep, to the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: hypnotic 把表示「睡眠」的希腊词根 hypn- 接上形容词词尾 -ic。

latinIntro.en: The new medical Latin of the eighteen hundreds borrowed Greek hypnos and built hypnotismus, from which English took hypnotic.
latinIntro.cn: 十九世纪的新拉丁语医学借用了希腊语 hypnos，造出 hypnotismus，英语由此得到 hypnotic。

items.example: The root hypn- carries the image of falling asleep.
items.exampleCN: 词根 hypn- 带有入睡的画面。

items.example: Hypnos is pictured with poppies in his hand.
items.exampleCN: 许普诺斯手中常被画着罂粟花。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns a noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix -sis forms hypnosis, a sleep state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -sis 构成 hypnosis，表示睡眠状态。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms hypnotize, to make hypnotic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 hypnotize，意为使之进入催眠。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms hypnotist, a sleep-worker.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 hypnotist，表示从事催眠的人。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms hypnotism, the practice itself.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ism 构成 hypnotism，指催眠术本身。

items.example: The prefix hypo- belongs to a different family of words.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 hypo- 属于另一组词，不要与 hypn- 混淆。

latinEntries.example: Greek hypnos gives the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 hypnos 提供了整个词族的基础。

latinEntries.example: Medical Latin turned hypnos into hypnoticus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 医学拉丁语把 hypnos 变成 hypnoticus。

latinEntries.example: Hypnotismus is the direct model for English hypnotic.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hypnotismus 是英语 hypnotic 的直接样板。

definition_zh: 虚伪的；假仁假义的；言行不一的
definition_en: pretending to have good feelings or beliefs that you do not really have
core_image: 戴着一张笑脸面具，面具后却是另一副表情
scene: 台上的人高谈良心与慷慨，台下却把善款塞进自己口袋。It was hypocritical of the speaker to preach honesty while hiding the donations.
sceneCN: 这里 hypocritical 是「虚伪的、言行不一的」（第 1 个义项：假装拥有自己并没有的美德）；句意：讲者一边大谈诚信一边私吞捐款，真是虚伪。

pos.zh: 虚伪的；假仁假义的；言行不一的

derivatives.zh: 希腊语 hypo-（在下面）与 krinein（判断、演戏）合成，义为「虚伪；伪善」
由希腊语 hypocrites（演员）变来，义为「伪君子」
形容词加 -ally 构成的副词，义为「虚伪地」
形容词加 -ness（性质）构成的名词，义为「虚伪」

senses.title: Pretending to have virtues
senses.definition: putting on feelings of kindness or honesty that one does not actually have
senses.definitionCN: 装出自己并不真正拥有的善意或诚信
senses.example: It is hypocritical to demand silence and then talk loudly yourself.
senses.exampleCN: 要求别人安静而自己大声说话，是虚伪的。
senses.why: Greek hypokrites meant an actor on a stage, so the word begins with the image of a mask worn in public.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 hypokrites 指舞台上的演员，所以这个词一开始就带着「公开戴面具」的画面。

senses.title: Saying one thing and doing another
senses.titleCN: 言行不一的；说一套做一套的
senses.definition: criticizing in others exactly what one does oneself
senses.definitionCN: 责备别人的正是自己也在做的事
senses.example: He gave a hypocritical warning about wasting paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他关于浪费纸张的警告实在言行不一。
senses.why: When the actor drops the mask mid scene, what remains is a plain mismatch between words and acts.
senses.whyCN: 当演员在戏中途摘下假面，剩下的就是言语与行为之间赤裸裸的不一致。

senses.title: Feigned in a passing way
senses.definition: showing affection or concern that is not really felt
senses.definitionCN: 表现出并无真实情感的关爱或关切
senses.example: She offered a hypocritical smile and looked away.
senses.exampleCN: 她挤出一个不真诚的微笑，然后转过脸去。
senses.why: The stage image narrows into small daily performances: a smile worn only for the moment.
senses.whyCN: 舞台画面收窄为日常的小型表演：只为此刻戴上的笑容。

intro.en: Hypocritical grows from Greek hypokrites, a stage actor answering under a mask, through hypokrisis, acting on stage, and later hypocrisy.
intro.cn: hypocritical 由希腊语 hypokrites（戴面具在台下应答的演员）经 hypokrisis（舞台表演）发展到 hypocrisy 而来。

items.en: Hypokrites is first an actor who answers on the stage.
items.cn: hypokrites 最初指在舞台上作应答的演员。

items.en: Hypokrisis means acting, the very work of playing a part.
items.cn: hypokrisis 意为表演，指扮演角色的那份行当。

items.en: The word shifts from acting to false pretence in speech.
items.cn: 这个词从「演戏」转为言语上的虚假做作。

items.en: Latin hypocrisis borrows the term for a feigned manner.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语借入 hypocrisis，表示伪装的态度。

items.en: Hypocrisy names false show in English writings.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 hypocrisy，指虚假的做派。

items.en: The adjective hypocritical adds -al to the noun.
items.cn: 现代英语在名词后加 -al 得到形容词 hypocritical。

note.en: Hypocritical belongs to the family of hypocrisy, hypocrite, and hypocrisy-derived forms, and neighbours words for insincerity and mere imitation.
note.cn: hypocritical 属于 hypocrisy、hypocrite 的词族，并与「不真诚」和「单纯模仿」两类词相邻。

entries.definition: the practice of pretending to be better than one is
a person who puts on a false show of virtue
in a false, pretence-full way
imagined for the sake of argument; only looks similar, different root
entries.definitionCN: 假设的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: not expressing real feelings
saying one thing to one person and another behind their back
showing moral goodness in a false, showy way

normalIntro.en: Hypocritical is the adjective of the actor family: hypocrisy, hypocrite, and the mask behind the smile.
normalIntro.cn: hypocritical 是「演员词族」的形容词：hypocrisy、hypocrite，以及笑容背后的那副面具。

normal.en: Greek hypokrites means an actor, and an actor wears a mask.
normal.cn: 希腊语 hypokrites 意为演员，而演员要戴面具。

normal.en: The noun hypocrisy means the false show, and -al makes it an adjective.
normal.cn: 名词 hypocrisy 表示虚假的做派，加上 -al 就成为形容词。

normal.en: Hypocrite names the person who does not practise what they preach.
normal.cn: hypocrite 指那些说一套做一套的人。

normal.en: Hypocritically is the adverb, used for the manner in which such a person acts.
normal.cn: hypocritically 是副词，用来形容这类人做事的方式。

normal.en: Compare hypocritical with sincere: the first wears a mask, the latter has none.
normal.cn: 对比 hypocritical 与 sincere：前者戴着面具，后者坦露真容。

abstract.en: Picture a smiling mask hanging beside a frowning face.
abstract.cn: 想象一张笑脸面具挂在皱眉的面孔旁边。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand pointing at another while its own palm is dirty.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手指着别人，自己的手掌却脏兮兮。

abstract.en: Think of a speech about honesty written by a thief.
abstract.cn: 想象一篇讲诚信的稿子出自小偷之手。

examples.en: Criticizing her for being late was a bit hypocritical when you were late too.
examples.cn: 你自己也迟到了，还批评她迟到，有点虚伪。

examples.en: The company made a hypocritical promise to cut waste while printing far more paper.
examples.cn: 公司一边承诺减少浪费，一边印了多得多的纸，十分虚伪。

examples.en: Nobody trusted his hypocritical kindness any more.
examples.cn: 再也没人相信他那虚伪的好意了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西部克利提克」——西部片里的反派提起酒杯笑呵呵，背后却藏着一把刀；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hypo-（在下面）＋ krites（判断、评判者），原指在台下应答的演员 hypokrites → 拉丁语 hypocrisis → 英语 hypocrisy、hypocrite，再加 -al 得到 hypocritical，核心义「用表演代替真实」。

sensesIntro.en: Hypocritical begins with the masked actor, shifts to the gap between words and deeds, and ends with small insincere performances of daily life.
sensesIntro.cn: hypocritical 从戴面具的演员出发，转到言语与行为之间的落差，最后落到日常生活中那些不真诚的小表演。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smiling mask worn over a different face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张笑脸面具盖着另一副面孔。

branches.en: The virtue that is only performed is the mask on stage.
branches.cn: 只被表演出来的美德就是舞台上的面具。

branches.en: The gap between speech and conduct is the actor forgetting the script.
branches.cn: 言与行的落差就像演员忘了台词。

branches.en: A temporary false smile is a brief mask put on for a moment.
branches.cn: 一时的假笑是随手戴上的小小面具。

branches.en: A person praised for honesty who lies is both mask and mismatch.
branches.cn: 被称赞诚实却撒谎的人，既戴面具又言行不一。

branches.en: Small polite fakes and outright lies differ only in scale.
branches.cn: 小小的客套假相与彻底的谎言只是程度不同。

intro.en: Hypocritical is hypo- plus the judging root crit- plus -al: a judgement given from under a mask.
intro.cn: hypocritical 由 hypo-、表示「判断」的词根 crit- 与词尾 -al 组成：从面具下做出的判断。

latinIntro.en: Latin hypocrisis, borrowed from Greek, gave English hypocrisy and hypocrite, and the adjective came by adding -al.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hypocrisis 借自希腊语，给了英语 hypocrisy 与 hypocrite，再加 -al 得到形容词。

items.example: The prefix hypo- means below the surface.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 hypo- 表示表层之下。

items.example: The root crit- runs through critic and crisis.
items.exampleCN: 词根 crit- 贯穿 critic 与 crisis。

items.example: The suffix -ic makes nouns into adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 把名词变为形容词。

items.example: The suffix -al turns hypocrite into hypocritical.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把 hypocrite 变成 hypocritical。

items.example: The suffix -y forms hypocrisy, the state itself.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 hypocrisy，指那种状态本身。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms hypocritically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 hypocritically。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms hypocriticalness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 hypocriticalness。

items.example: The same prefix also opens hypothesis and hypothetical.
items.exampleCN: 同一前缀也引出 hypothesis 与 hypothetical。

definition_zh: 低血压；低血压症
definition_en: a condition in which the blood pressure is lower than normal
core_image: 水管里的水压过低，水端不上二楼
scene: 病人刚站起来就头晕眼花，护士连忙量了血压。After a short fever the patient had temporary hypotension and needed to sit down slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 hypotension 是「低血压」（第 1 个义项：血压低于正常水平）；句意：一场短热之后病人出现暂时性低血压，需要慢慢地坐下。

pos.zh: 低血压；低血压症

derivatives.zh: hypo-（低于）与 tensio（张力）加形容词词尾构成的，义为「低血压的」
同一词根换前缀 hyper-（超过），义为「高血压」
拉丁语 tendere（拉伸）的名词形式，义为「张力；压力」

senses.title: Low blood pressure
senses.definition: blood pressure that stays lower than the normal range
senses.definitionCN: 低于正常范围的血压
senses.example: The nurse noted hypotension before the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术前护士记录到低血压。
senses.why: Hypo- means under, and tension is the pull of the blood in the vessels, so the word pictures the pressure as too weak.
senses.whyCN: hypo- 表示「在下面」，tension 是血液在血管里的张力，于是这个词把压力画得太小。

senses.title: A drop that makes you dizzy
senses.definition: a sudden fall of blood pressure that causes dizziness or fainting
senses.definitionCN: 血压突然下降，引起头晕或昏厥
senses.example: Orthostatic hypotension hit her each time she stood up.
senses.exampleCN: 每次起身，体位性低血压就让她一阵头晕。
senses.why: Standing up changes the pull of blood at once, and this falling pressure is the most familiar picture of the word.
senses.whyCN: 起身的一瞬间血液的张力立刻改变，这种下降的压力正是这个词最常见的画面。

senses.title: A medical classification
senses.titleCN: 临床分类中的低血压症
senses.definition: a clinical label used for readouts and for graded cases
senses.definitionCN: 检查读数与病例分级时使用的临床标签
senses.example: The chart listed hypotension as the only abnormal finding.
senses.exampleCN: 病历上只把低血压列为异常发现。
senses.why: The word lives mainly in the medical chart and is a technical label more than an everyday word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词主要活在病历与检查单里，更像技术标签而不是日常用语。

senses.title: A side effect of treatment
senses.definition: pressure that falls because of drugs, bleeding, or anaesthesia
senses.definitionCN: 因药物、失血或麻醉而下降的血压
senses.example: Severe hypotension followed the blood loss.
senses.exampleCN: 失血之后出现了严重低血压。
senses.why: The prefix sets only the direction of the pressure, and the reason for it is left open, so it also names such unwanted drops.
senses.whyCN: 前缀只说明压力的方向，原因留空，因此也用来指这种不想要的下降。

senses.title: A body condition to watch
senses.definition: a condition that needs monitoring during care
senses.definitionCN: 在护理中需要持续监测的状况
senses.example: Monitoring hypotension is a daily task in intensive care.
senses.exampleCN: 在重症监护中监测低血压是每天的工作。
senses.why: As the word spreads into nursing notes, it also names the condition as a thing to watch rather than a single reading.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入护理记录后，也指需要盯着看的状态，而不再是单次读数。

intro.en: Hypotension is a modern scientific compound of Greek hypo-, under, Latin tensio, a stretching or tension, and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: hypotension 是近代科学构词，由希腊语 hypo-（在下）、拉丁语 tensio（拉伸、张力）和名词词尾 -ion 合成。

items.en: Hypo- means under or less than, as in hypodermic.
items.cn: hypo- 意为在下、少于，如 hypodermic。

items.en: Tendere means to stretch, and tensio means a stretching or tension.
items.cn: tendere 意为拉伸，tensio 意为拉伸、张力。

items.en: Medical writers join hypo- with the tension root for low pressure.
items.cn: 医学作者把 hypo- 与「张力」词根结合，表示低压力。

items.en: The word appears with the growth of blood pressure measurement.
items.cn: 随着血压测量的发展，英语中出现了这个词。

items.en: Its opposite hypertension enters English in the same period.
items.cn: 它的反义词 hypertension 在同一时期进入英语。

note.en: Hypotension is built on the tension root with hypo-, and faces the pressure words hypertension, presyncope, and shock.
note.cn: hypotension 由 hypo- 与「张力」词根构成，正面对着 hypertension、presyncope、shock 等压力词。

entries.definition: high blood pressure; the prefix hyper- reverses hypo-
entries.definitionCN: 高血压；前缀 hyper- 与 hypo- 相反

entries.definition: of, or tending to lower, blood pressure
dangerously low body temperature; shares hypo- only
entries.definitionCN: 低体温；只共享前缀 hypo-

entries.definition: a proposed explanation; only looks similar, different root
entries.definitionCN: 假设；只是拼写相近，词根不同

entries.definition: a near fainting feeling often caused by low pressure
the dizzy feeling of a falling blood supply to the brain
the dangerous failure of the body to keep pressure up

normalIntro.en: Hypotension is hypo-, meaning under, plus tension, the pull of blood in the vessels: pressure below the normal line.
normalIntro.cn: hypotension 是 hypo-（低于）加上 tension（血管里血液的张力）：压力掉在正常线以下。

normal.en: Greek hypo- means under, like the hypodermal layer under the skin.
normal.cn: 希腊语前缀 hypo- 意为在下，如皮肤下的 hypodermal。

normal.en: The root tendere means to stretch, which gives tension and the pressure idea.
normal.cn: 词根 tendere 意为拉伸，由此得到 tension 以及压力的概念。

normal.en: Swap the prefix for hyper- and hypotension becomes hypertension.
normal.cn: 把前缀换成 hyper-，hypotension 就变成 hypertension。

normal.en: The matching adjective is hypotensive, used for drugs that lower pressure.
normal.cn: 对应的形容词是 hypotensive，常用来形容降压药。

normal.en: Compare presyncope, which names the dizzy feeling that low pressure brings.
normal.cn: 对比 presyncope，它专指低血压引起的那种晕眩感。

abstract.en: Picture a water pipe whose stream cannot reach the second floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一根水管水流太弱，怎么也送不到二楼。

abstract.en: Imagine standing up and the room going grey for a second.
abstract.cn: 想象一站起来，眼前的世界灰了一瞬。

abstract.en: Think of the mark on a gauge that stays just under the safe line.
abstract.cn: 想象仪表指针总停在安全线下方一点点。

examples.en: Doctors watched for hypotension after the anaesthetic.
examples.cn: 麻醉之后医生们密切观察低血压。

examples.en: Chronic hypotension can leave people feeling tired all day.
examples.cn: 慢性低血压会让人整天觉得疲惫。

examples.en: The drug may cause mild hypotension in older patients.
examples.cn: 该药物可能使年长患者出现轻度低血压。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕欧藤逊」——水一怕、油一冷，水管里的藤蔓也绷不紧，压力就低了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hypo-（在下、低于）＋ 拉丁语 tendere / tensio（拉紧、张力）＋ 名词词尾 -ion → hypotension，核心义「张力低于正常」。

sensesIntro.en: Hypotension begins as a reading below normal, becomes the dizziness of a sudden drop, and settles into the technical label of health care.
sensesIntro.cn: hypotension 先是低于正常的读数，随后指突然下降带来的头晕，最后固定为医疗领域的技术标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a water pipe whose pressure is too weak.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根水压太弱的水管。

branches.en: A reading under the normal line is the plain medical sense.
branches.cn: 低于正常线的读数是最基本的医学义项。

branches.en: A drop that makes the head spin is the pipe losing water for a moment.
branches.cn: 让人头晕的下降就像水管瞬间断流。

branches.en: The chart label is the pressure turned into a grading term.
branches.cn: 病历标签是把压力变成分级术语。

branches.en: A side effect and a condition to watch both come from the same low reading.
branches.cn: 副作用与需监护的状态都来自同一个低读数。

branches.en: A drug-induced fall is a low reading with a known cause.
branches.cn: 药物引起的下降就是一个有明确原因的低读数。

intro.en: Hypotension is a scientific compound: hypo- says below, and the tension root says tension, so the ending -ion marks a state.
intro.cn: hypotension 是科学构词：hypo- 说「低于」，tension 词根说「张力」，词尾 -ion 标记一种状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere and tensio supply the tension half, while Greek hypo- supplies the direction, and medical Latin fixed -ion for the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 与 tensio 提供「张力」那一半，希腊语 hypo- 提供方向，医学拉丁语用 -ion 固定为名词。

items.example: The prefix hypo- says the pressure falls short.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 hypo- 说明压力不足。

items.example: The prefix hyper- gives the opposite, hypertension.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 hyper- 给出反义词 hypertension。

items.example: The root tens- appears in tension and tensile.
items.exampleCN: 词根 tens- 出现在 tension 与 tensile 中。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成表示状态的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms hypotensive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 hypotensive。

items.example: The suffix -emia appears in anaemia and hypovolemia.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -emia 出现在 anaemia 与 hypovolemia 中。

items.example: The root cardio- is the heart as a machine.
items.exampleCN: 词根 cardio- 指作为机器的心脏。

items.example: Tension is the plain English half of the word.
items.exampleCN: tension 是这个单词的普通英语那一半。

definition_zh: 图标；偶像；崇拜对象；典型象征
definition_en: a small picture on a screen, a widely admired person, or a sacred image
core_image: 一尊镶金的小画像被举在教堂中央，人人抬头凝望
scene: 教堂正中的木架上供着一幅金边小画像，信众排着长队上前亲吻它。At Easter the worshippers file past the painted icon in the church.
sceneCN: 这里 icon 是「圣像、神圣画像」（第 3 个义项：东正教里供人敬拜的画像）；句意：复活节时信众排队走过教堂里那幅彩绘圣像。

pos.zh: 图标；偶像；圣像；象征

derivatives.zh: 偶像级的；标志性的
图像学；图像符号体系
破坏圣像者；反传统者
破坏传统观念的

senses.title: A small picture on a screen
senses.definition: a small symbol on a computer screen that you click to open a program or file
senses.definitionCN: 电脑屏幕上可点击的小符号，用来打开程序或文件
senses.example: Click the printer icon to start printing.
senses.exampleCN: 点击打印机图标开始打印。
senses.why: Greek eikon meant an image, so the little picture that stands for a program is a direct heir of the sacred image.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 eikon 本义就是「图像」，代表某个程序的小画片正是「圣像」意象的直接后裔。

senses.title: An admired public figure
senses.definition: a person or thing that is greatly admired and comes to stand for an era or a group
senses.definitionCN: 备受崇拜、并成为某个时代或群体象征的人物或事物
senses.example: She became an icon of the fashion world.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了时尚界的偶像。
senses.why: Someone people look up to is treated almost like a sacred image set on a wall.
senses.whyCN: 被众人仰望的人物，几乎就像被挂在墙上的圣像，于是「偶像」义由此生长。

senses.title: A sacred painted image
senses.definition: a painted image of a holy figure that believers venerate, especially in the Orthodox Church
senses.definitionCN: 东正教等教会中供信众敬拜的圣者画像
senses.example: The old icon hangs above the altar.
senses.exampleCN: 一幅古老的圣像挂在祭坛上方。
senses.why: This is the earliest sense, from Byzantine Greek eikon, a likeness or image of a holy person.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早的义项，来自拜占庭希腊语 eikon，即圣者的画像或形貌。

senses.title: A symbol standing for an idea
senses.definition: something widely seen as the symbol of a quality, belief, or way of life
senses.definitionCN: 被广泛视为某种品质、信念或生活方式的象征物
senses.example: The red bus is an icon of London.
senses.exampleCN: 红色双层巴士是伦敦的标志。
senses.why: Once an image can stand for a person, it can stand for a whole city or idea.
senses.whyCN: 既然图像能代表一个人，也就能代表整座城市或某种观念，象征义由此扩展而来。

senses.title: A distinctive graphic sign
senses.definition: a simple drawing used in public signs, maps, or symbols to convey information quickly
senses.definitionCN: 用在公共标志、地图上快速传达信息的简单图形
senses.example: The map uses small icons for cafés and restrooms.
senses.exampleCN: 地图用小图形符号标出咖啡馆和洗手间。
senses.why: Any compact picture that carries a message follows the same image logic as the screen icon.
senses.whyCN: 任何承载信息的紧凑画片，都沿用了与屏幕图标相同的「图像表意」逻辑。

intro.en: Icon comes from Greek eikon, a likeness or image, later narrowed to a sacred portrait, and widened again by computing.
intro.cn: icon 来自希腊语 eikon（形貌、图像），先收窄为圣像，又在计算机时代重新拓宽。

items.en: Eikon means a likeness or image.
items.cn: 希腊语 eikon 意为形貌或图像。

items.en: Latin takes icon as an image or a portrait.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 icon，指图像或肖像。

items.en: The word comes to mean a sacred painted portrait used in worship.
items.cn: 这个词转指礼拜用的圣像画。

items.en: English borrows icon for a religious image.
items.cn: 英语借入 icon，指宗教图像。

items.en: Icon extends to an admired person and to a screen symbol.
items.cn: icon 扩展到受敬仰的人物与屏幕符号。

note.en: Icon and its family (iconic, iconoclast, iconography) sit close to ideal, idol, and emblems of symbolism.
note.cn: icon 及同族词 iconic、iconoclast、iconography 与 ideal、idol 以及各类象征词相邻。

entries.definition: widely recognised as a symbol of something
entries.definitionCN: 标志性的；被普遍认作象征的

entries.definition: a person who attacks established beliefs or images
entries.definitionCN: 攻击传统观念或破坏圣像的人

entries.definition: the visual images and symbols of a subject
an image or person that is worshipped
a sign that represents something else
a distinctive badge or sign of a group

normalIntro.en: Icon is an image that has gathered meaning: once it stood for a saint, now it stands for a program or a star.
normalIntro.cn: icon 是「积攒了意义的图像」：过去代表圣徒，如今代表一个程序或一位明星。

normal.en: On a phone, click an icon to open an app.
normal.cn: 在手机上，点击图标即可打开应用。

normal.en: An icon can be a person, as in a style icon.
normal.cn: icon 也可以指人，如「时尚偶像」。

normal.en: A national icon is something a whole country claims as its symbol.
normal.cn: 民族象征是被整个国家认作标志的事物。

normal.en: Iconic adds -ic and means having the quality of an icon.
normal.cn: iconic 加词尾 -ic，表示具有 icon 的特质。

normal.en: Compare symbol: a symbol is abstract, an icon is also a concrete picture.
normal.cn: 对比 symbol：symbol 是抽象符号，icon 同时是具体的图像。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny gold-framed picture above a church door.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅镶金边的小画挂在教堂门楣上。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole crowd turning their eyes to one face.
abstract.cn: 想象整群人把目光投向同一个面孔。

abstract.en: Think of a small square on a screen that quietly points to everything behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上的一个小方块，安静地指向它背后的一切。

examples.en: The icon on the desktop stands for the shared folder.
examples.cn: 桌面上的图标代表共享文件夹。

examples.en: Many young players treat him as an icon of the sport.
examples.cn: 很多年轻球员把他当作这项运动的偶像。

examples.en: Restorers cleaned the painted icon with great care.
examples.cn: 修复师小心翼翼地清理那幅彩绘圣像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱看」——大家「爱看」的画片先是圣像，后来成了屏幕上的小图标；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 eikon（形貌、图像）→ 拉丁语 icon（肖像、图像）→ 拜占庭希腊语「圣像」→ 英语 icon。核心义「图像」，图像被赋予意义即成图标、偶像与象征。

sensesIntro.en: Icon starts as a sacred image, then grows into an admired person, a sign of an era, a quick graphic, and finally a clickable picture on a screen.
sensesIntro.cn: icon 从圣像出发，先长成受人仰望的偶像，再成为时代象征、图形符号，最后变成屏幕上可点击的小图标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small framed image that everyone lifts their eyes to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅人人都抬头凝望的小画像。

branches.en: The sacred painted image is the oldest layer.
branches.cn: 圣像画是最古老的一层意义。

branches.en: An admired figure is a living icon.
branches.cn: 受敬仰的人物是「活着的圣像」。

branches.en: The screen icon is the newest image sense.
branches.cn: 屏幕图标是最新的「图像」义项。

branches.en: A symbol or national emblem carries the idea outward to a whole culture.
branches.cn: 象征与民族标志把「图像代表某物」的观念推向整个文化。

branches.en: Both the screen icon and the map graphic are compact pictures that carry information.
branches.cn: 屏幕图标与地图图形都是承载信息的紧凑画片。

intro.en: Icon is a Greek loanword whose family grows with the suffixes -ic, -ography, and -clast.
intro.cn: icon 是希腊语借词，其后缀 -ic、-ography、-clast 各生出同族词。

latinIntro.en: The word came through Latin icon from Greek eikon, but the living roots are Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经拉丁语 icon 借入英语，真正的词根却来自希腊语 eikon。

items.example: Eikon is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: eikon 是英语词的直接祖先。

items.example: Latin icon carried the word into the West.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 icon 把这个词带入西方。

items.example: English icon keeps all the image senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语 icon 保留了全部「图像」义。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms iconic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 iconic。

items.example: Iconic describes things that stand for a culture.
items.exampleCN: iconic 形容能代表一种文化的事物。

items.example: The element -ography builds iconography.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -ography 构成 iconography。

items.example: The element -clast builds iconoclast.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -clast 构成 iconoclast。

items.meaning: a breaker of images or old beliefs
items.example: Iconoclast splits into image and breaker.
items.exampleCN: iconoclast 由「图像」和「破坏者」两部分组成。

items.example: Iconography studies the images of an age.
items.exampleCN: 图像学研究一个时代的图像。

definition_zh: 可辨认的；可识别的；可确定的
definition_en: able to be recognised, named, or clearly seen as a particular thing
core_image: 人群中一个戴红围巾的人被一眼认出来
scene: 监控画面很模糊，但警方仍能从身形和步态中认出那个嫌疑人。Even in the blurred footage the suspect remains identifiable by his walk.
sceneCN: 这里 identifiable 是「可辨认的」（第 1 个义项：能够被认出是谁或是什么）；句意：即使画面模糊，那个嫌疑人仍能凭走路的姿态被辨认出来。

pos.zh: 可辨认的；可识别的；可确定的

derivatives.zh: 辨认；确定；认同
辨认；身份证明
身份；同一性
无法辨认的

senses.title: Able to be recognised
senses.definition: able to be recognised as a particular person or thing among others
senses.definitionCN: 在众多人或物中能够被认出是哪一个
senses.example: The thief was identifiable from the security footage.
senses.exampleCN: 窃贼可以从监控录像中被辨认出来。
senses.why: Identify comes from Latin idem, the same, so something identifiable can be matched to the one it truly is.
senses.whyCN: identify 源于拉丁语 idem（同一），所以「可辨认」就是能与它真正的那个「同一」对上的意思。

senses.title: Able to be named or pointed out
senses.definition: able to be named explicitly or pointed out as a specific example
senses.definitionCN: 能够被明确点名或作为具体例子指出来的
senses.example: The report names three identifiable causes of the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出了三个明确的延误原因。
senses.why: If you can recognise something, you can also name it, so the word extends to things that can be cited.
senses.whyCN: 能认出某物，也就能说出它的名字，于是义项扩展到「可明确指名」的事物。

senses.title: Perceptible or clear
senses.definition: strong or clear enough to be noticed or perceived
senses.definitionCN: 强到或清楚到足以被人注意到、感知到
senses.example: There was an identifiable change in her tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她的语气有明显的变化。
senses.why: What can be picked out also stands out, giving the weaker sense of merely being noticeable.
senses.whyCN: 能被挑出来的东西自然也显眼，于是弱化为「可察觉、看得出来」的意思。

senses.title: Able to be established
senses.definition: possible to establish or confirm with certainty, especially a fact, cause, or risk
senses.definitionCN: 能够被确切认定或证实的，尤指事实、原因或风险
senses.example: No identifiable cause for the failure has been found.
senses.exampleCN: 尚未找到可以确定的原因。
senses.why: To identify in modern usage also means to establish a fact, so identifiable covers what can be pinned down.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法里 identify 也表示「认定事实」，因此 identifiable 覆盖了「能够被确定下来」的情形。

intro.en: Identifiable is identify plus -able; identify comes from Medieval Latin identificare, built on idem, the same.
intro.cn: identifiable 由 identify 加 -able 构成；identify 来自中世纪拉丁语 identificare，其词根是 idem（同一）。

items.en: Idem means the same.
items.cn: 拉丁语 idem 意为同一。

items.en: Identificare, a scholastic term, names making something the same.
items.cn: 经院哲学术语 identificare 指使某物相同。

items.en: French identique carries the idea of sameness.
items.cn: 法语 identique 承载「相同」的观念。

items.en: Identify appears and later means to recognise who someone is.
items.cn: identify 进入英语，后来获得「认出是谁」的意思。

items.en: The suffix -able adds the sense of being recognisable.
items.cn: 词尾 -able 加上「能够被」的意思，形成 identifiable。

note.en: Identifiable belongs to the identify family and sits near recognisable, discernible, and distinguishable.
note.cn: identifiable 属于 identify 词族，与 recognisable、discernible、distinguishable 意义相邻。

entries.definition: to recognise or establish who or what something is
in exactly the same way
the act of recognising or proving who someone is
easy to know because you have seen it before
possible to see or notice, though not obvious
possible to tell apart from something else

normalIntro.en: Identifiable is the -able form of identify, so it always asks whether a thing can be picked out and matched to one name.
normalIntro.cn: identifiable 是 identify 带 -able 的形式，所以它总在问：这种东西能否被挑出来并对应到一个名字。

normal.en: Easily identifiable means people can spot it at once.
normal.cn: easily identifiable 表示人们一眼就能认出。

normal.en: The prefix id- is the Latin idem, meaning the same.
normal.cn: 前缀 id- 来自拉丁语 idem，意为同一。

normal.en: The suffix -able turns a verb into an adjective of possibility.
normal.cn: 词尾 -able 把动词变成表示「能够被」的形容词。

normal.en: Identifiable features are the marks that make a person or thing stand out.
normal.cn: 可辨识的特征就是让某人某物与众不同的标记。

normal.en: Compare identify: the verb is the action, identifiable is the property.
normal.cn: 对比 identify：动词是动作，identifiable 是性质。

abstract.en: Picture one red scarf in a crowd dressed in grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一片灰衣人群中唯一的红围巾。

abstract.en: Imagine a name tag that fits only one face in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只对得上房间里某一张脸的名牌。

abstract.en: Think of a step that everyone can hear coming from far away.
abstract.cn: 想象一种脚步声，远远就能被听出是谁。

examples.en: The letters are not identifiable without a microscope.
examples.cn: 不用显微镜就看不清这些字母是什么。

examples.en: Researchers found no identifiable link between diet and the illness.
examples.cn: 研究者没有发现饮食与这种疾病之间有明确的关联。

examples.en: Every suspect was identifiable by the colour of his jacket.
examples.cn: 每个嫌疑人凭外套颜色都能被认出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱猜得否」——见到的人要「猜得出来、认得出」，就是可辨认的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 idem（同一）→ 中世纪拉丁语 identificare（使相同）→ 英语 identify → identify + -able → identifiable。核心义「能与本尊对上」，故为可辨认、可确定。

sensesIntro.en: Identifiable starts from being able to match a thing to its own name, then widens to what can be named, noticed, and finally established as fact.
sensesIntro.cn: identifiable 先从「能与本尊对上」出发，再放宽为可指名、可察觉，最后扩展到可被认定为事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one red scarf that everyone can pick out of a grey crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰衣人群里人人都能挑出的那条红围巾。

branches.en: Being able to recognise it is the core sense.
branches.cn: 能被认出是核心义项。

branches.en: Being able to name it is the citing sense.
branches.cn: 能被指名是引证用法。

branches.en: Being noticeable is the weak perceptual sense.
branches.cn: 可被察觉是较弱的感知义。

branches.en: Being established as fact is the modern administrative sense.
branches.cn: 可被确定为事实是现代行政语境下的义项。

branches.en: Both recognition and confirmation rest on matching a thing to what it truly is.
branches.cn: 辨认与确认都建立在「事物与它的本来面目对上」这一点上。

intro.en: Identifiable is identify plus the suffix -able, with -ate and -fy hidden in the verb itself.
intro.cn: identifiable 是 identify 加词尾 -able，而动词里还藏着 -ate 与 -fy 的痕迹。

latinIntro.en: The family goes back to Latin idem, the same, through the medieval verb identificare.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族经中世纪拉丁语动词 identificare 追溯至拉丁语 idem（同一）。

items.example: Idem is the deep root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: idem 是整族词的深层词根。

items.example: The Latin element -ficare meant to make.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语成分 -ficare 意为使成为。

items.example: Identify is the verb at the head of the family.
items.exampleCN: identify 是这个词族的核心动词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms identifiable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 identifiable。

items.example: Identifiable describes people or facts that can be pinned down.
items.exampleCN: identifiable 形容能被认定的人或事实。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms the noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成表示行为的抽象名词。

items.example: Identity shares the same idem root.
items.exampleCN: identity 与它共享 idem 词根。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unidentifiable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unidentifiable。

items.example: The suffix -ical builds identical.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ical 构成 identical。

definition_zh: 田园诗般的；宁静优美的；质朴宜人的
definition_en: peaceful, beautiful, and simple in a way that seems like a perfect country scene
core_image: 一条小溪绕过绿草坡，几头羊在树荫下慢慢吃草
scene: 假期里他们住进山间小屋，每天早上都被鸟鸣和溪水声叫醒。They spent a week in a small village where the mornings felt completely idyllic.
sceneCN: 这里 idyllic 是「田园诗般的、宁静美好的」（第 1 个义项：像画中的乡村景致一样安详美丽）；句意：他们在一个小村庄住了一周，每天早晨都像田园诗一样安详。

pos.zh: 田园诗般的；宁静优美的

derivatives.zh: 田园诗；牧歌式的短诗或情景
如田园诗般地
偶像；神像（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

senses.title: Like a peaceful rural scene
senses.definition: charmingly simple and peaceful, like an ideal picture of country life
senses.definitionCN: 质朴安详、像理想中的乡村生活图景一样动人
senses.example: The cottage stood in an idyllic valley.
senses.exampleCN: 小屋坐落在一条如画的河谷中。
senses.why: Greek eidyllion meant a little picture or short poem, so idyllic means having the charm of such a little country picture.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 eidyllion 指小图画或小诗，所以 idyllic 就是「具有这种乡村小画般魅力」的意思。

senses.title: Happy and untroubled
senses.definition: so happy and free of trouble that it seems unreal
senses.definitionCN: 幸福而无忧，近乎不真实
senses.example: She describes an idyllic childhood on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 她描述了一个在海岸边度过的幸福童年。
senses.why: The poem of country life is also a poem of easy days, so the word slips from scenery to untroubled experience.
senses.whyCN: 田园诗既是写景，也是写悠闲日子，所以这个词从景致滑向无忧无虑的生活体验。

senses.title: Perfectly suited
senses.definition: perfectly suitable or pleasant, often said of conditions
senses.definitionCN: 极为合适或惬意的，常用来形容各种条件
senses.example: The mild weather made it an idyllic day for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 温和的天气使它成为野餐的理想日子。
senses.why: Once idyllic means picture perfect, it can praise any condition that feels just right.
senses.whyCN: 既然 idyllic 表示「画一般完美」，它就可以用来称赞任何恰到好处的条件。

senses.title: Unrealistically ideal
senses.definition: idealised to the point of ignoring real problems or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 被理想化到忽略实际问题或艰辛的程度
senses.example: The film offers an idyllic view of village life.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片给出了一种过于理想化的乡村生活图景。
senses.why: A picture of perfection can also be a misleading one, so the word gains a faintly ironic edge.
senses.whyCN: 完美的图景也可能误导人，因此这个词带上了一丝反讽意味。

intro.en: Idyllic is formed from idyll, from Greek eidyllion, a little picture or short poem, later softened to country scenes.
intro.cn: idyllic 由 idyll 派生，idyll 来自希腊语 eidyllion（小图画、小诗），后来转指乡村景致。

items.en: Eidyllion is a small image or a short poem.
items.cn: 希腊语 eidyllion 意为小图像或小诗。

items.en: Idyllium names short pastoral poems.
items.cn: 拉丁语 idyllium 指短小的田园诗。

items.en: English borrows idyll for a pastoral poem.
items.cn: 英语借入 idyll，指田园短诗。

items.en: Idyll widens to any charmingly simple scene of life.
items.cn: idyll 扩展指任何质朴动人的生活场景。

items.en: The adjective idyllic grows from the noun.
items.cn: 形容词 idyllic 由这个名词派生而来。

note.en: Idyllic belongs to the idyll word family and sits close to pastoral, picturesque, and tranquil scene words.
note.cn: idyllic 属于 idyll 词族，与 pastoral、picturesque 以及表示宁静的描写词相邻。

entries.definition: a short poem or scene of simple country life
in a peaceful country way
an image or person that is worshipped
entries.definitionCN: 偶像；神像（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to do with shepherds and simple country life
pretty enough to be painted
calm and free from noise

normalIntro.en: Idyllic is the adjective of idyll, a little country poem or picture, so it always carries a painted pasture in it.
normalIntro.cn: idyllic 是 idyll（小小的乡村诗或画）的形容词，所以它总带着一幅田园小画。

normal.en: An idyllic village looks like a postcard.
normal.cn: 田园诗般的村庄看起来像一张明信片。

normal.en: An idyllic childhood is remembered as trouble free.
normal.cn: 幸福的童年被记成无忧无虑。

normal.en: The suffix -ic turns the noun idyll into an adjective.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ic 把名词 idyll 变成形容词。

normal.en: To say far from idyllic is to admit a place was not peaceful at all.
normal.cn: 说 far from idyllic 就是承认那地方一点都不安宁。

normal.en: Compare pastoral: pastoral describes shepherds and herds, idyllic describes a perfect little country picture.
normal.cn: 对比 pastoral：pastoral 侧重牧人与畜群，idyllic 侧重一幅完美的乡村小画。

abstract.en: Picture a stream curving past a green bank with slow sheep.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小溪绕过绿岸，羊群缓缓吃草。

abstract.en: Imagine a morning with birdsong and no clock.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只有鸟鸣、没有钟表的清晨。

abstract.en: Think of a picnic table under an apple tree on a mild day.
abstract.cn: 想象天气温和，苹果树下的野餐桌。

examples.en: The island is known for its idyllic beaches.
examples.cn: 这座岛以如画的沙滩闻名。

examples.en: They left the city for an idyllic life in the hills.
examples.cn: 他们离开城市，到山里过起了田园般的生活。

examples.en: The reality of farming is rarely idyllic.
examples.cn: 务农的现实很少像田园诗那般美好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱得悠闲」——在乡下「爱得悠闲」地看羊吃草，就是田园诗般的生活；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 eidyllion（小图像、小诗）→ 拉丁语 idyllium（田园短诗）→ 英语 idyll → idyll + -ic → idyllic。核心义「像一幅小小的田园画」。

sensesIntro.en: Idyllic starts from a picture of country peace, extends to untroubled happiness and ideal conditions, and sometimes turns ironic.
sensesIntro.cn: idyllic 从一幅宁静的乡村小画出发，扩展到无忧的幸福与理想的条件，有时还带上反讽色彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stream, a green slope, and sheep grazing in shade.
core.cn: 核心意象：小溪、绿坡与树荫下吃草的羊群。

branches.en: Peaceful rural charm is the core sense.
branches.cn: 宁静的乡村之美是核心义项。

branches.en: Untroubled happiness is the lived sense.
branches.cn: 无忧的幸福是从景致转到生活感受的义项。

branches.en: Ideal conditions are the extended praise sense.
branches.cn: 理想的条件是扩展后的称许义。

branches.en: Unrealistic perfection is the critical sense.
branches.cn: 过于理想化是带批评色彩的义项。

branches.en: A picture perfect day and a perfect place share the same painted calm.
branches.cn: 完美的一天与完美的地点共享同一种「画中安宁」。

intro.en: Idyllic is idyll plus -ic, while idyll itself is a softened Greek word for a tiny picture.
intro.cn: idyllic 是 idyll 加词尾 -ic；而 idyll 本身是希腊语中「小图画」一词的软化形式。

latinIntro.en: The chain runs from Greek eidyllion through Latin idyllium to English idyll.
latinIntro.cn: 这条词源链从希腊语 eidyllion 经拉丁语 idyllium 到英语 idyll。

items.meaning: a little image, a short poem
items.example: Eidyllion is the ultimate source.
items.exampleCN: eidyllion 是最终来源。

items.example: Latin idyllium passes the word to Europe.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 idyllium 把这词传给欧洲。

items.meaning: a poem or scene of simple country life
items.example: English idyll keeps the picture of country peace.
items.exampleCN: 英语 idyll 保留了乡村安宁的画面。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms idyllic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 idyllic。

items.example: Idyllic describes scenes that seem painted.
items.exampleCN: idyllic 形容看似画出来的景致。

items.example: The suffix -ically forms idyllically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ically 构成 idyllically。

items.example: Idyllically describes how a scene unfolds.
items.exampleCN: idyllically 描述场景展开的方式。

items.example: Picturesque shares the image idea without the same root.
items.exampleCN: picturesque 共享「图像」观念，但词根不同。
